title: Vibhishana's crossing
hook: the enemy's brother asks to be let in; the camp argues; Rama makes a vow

segments.voice: Yesterday: Vibhishana told Ravana the truth, was called a disgrace, and crossed the sea. Your line: I've come for refuge.

A war camp on a beach, the eve of battle. A figure appears in the sky above it, with four armed companions, and calls down: I'm the enemy king's brother, please let me in. Sugriva, king of the monkeys, doesn't hesitate. He goes straight to Rama: this is a trick. He's a rakshasa, Ravana's own brother, and he'll strike when we're not looking. Kill him, or send him away. The whole camp starts arguing.
screen: `A FIGURE IN THE SKY.` → `THIS IS A TRICK.` → `THE CAMP ARGUES.`

segments.voice: Rama asks his council, and Valmiki lets every voice speak. Angada says test him first. Others say send a spy, or question him closely. Jambavan is suspicious of the timing. Then Hanuman speaks, the one who has actually been inside Lanka. He came openly, not in disguise. I've watched his face, and I see no deceit in it. He knows Ravana's wrongs and has seen your strength. Accept him. Then Rama gives his answer. I can't turn away someone who comes as a friend, even if he has faults. And then something larger. Anyone who comes to me even once and says, I am yours, I give safety from every being. That is my vow. Sugriva still pushes back. Rama goes further. Even if it were Ravana himself, bring him in. In the Sri Vaishnava tradition of South India, this verse is treasured as a teaching on sharanagati, taking refuge, or surrender: the one who turns to God even once, sincerely, is held. Others read it more plainly, as the code of a good king toward someone asking for protection. Then Rama does something practical and startling. He has Vibhishana come down, sends for sea water, and pours it over his head, consecrating him king of Lanka, right there on the beach, before a single battle has been fought.
screen: `EVERY VOICE IN THE COUNCIL.` · `HANUMAN: I SEE NO DECEIT.` · `ANYONE WHO SAYS I AM YOURS.` · `KING OF LANKA, ON THE BEACH.` · then, large: `EVEN IF IT WERE RAVANA HIMSELF.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone who once came to you asking for help or a second chance, someone you weren't sure you could trust, and picture them at the edge of your camp without deciding anything about them. Let the door in your chest open by one inch; breathe in and notice the caution, breathe out and notice the welcome, and let both be there.
Vibhishana's crossing. The enemy's brother asks for refuge, the camp argues, and Rama vows safety to anyone who comes even once and says, I am yours.
Your line: even if it were Ravana. Tomorrow, Lanka in sight. Day six hundred thirty-eight, done.

howItsDone: In the Sri Vaishnava tradition the Vibhishana episode is taught as the model of śaraṇāgati, taking refuge, and Rama's vow in Yuddha Kanda 18 is recited and commented on as a central verse.

original.note: Sanskrit śaraṇāgati: coming for refuge, from śaraṇa, refuge or shelter, and āgati, arrival; a key word in Sri Vaishnava teaching.
